targetText: Between capitalist and communist society lies the period of the revolutionary transformation of the one into the other. Corresponding to this is also a political transition period in which the state can be nothing but the revolutionary dictatorship of the proletariat.
summary: Quoting Marx's Critique of the Gotha Programme, Lenin underscores that the transition from capitalism to fully developed communism requires a temporary revolutionary workers' state to overcome capitalist resistance and reorganize production.

targetText: Democracy for the vast majority of the people, and suppression by force, i.e., exclusion from democracy, of the exploiters and oppressors of the people: this is the change democracy undergoes during the transition from capitalism to communism.
summary: Lenin analyzes the qualitative transformation of democracy under the dictatorship of the proletariat: boundless democratic rights for the working-class majority accompanied by forceful suppression of the capitalist minority.

targetText: Only in communist society, when the resistance of the capitalists have disappeared, when there are no classes (i.e., when there is no distinction between the members of society as regards their relation to the social means of production), only then “the state... ceases to exist", and “it becomes possible to speak of freedom".
summary: Lenin explains that the coercive state apparatus can only wither away completely once class distinctions disappear and social cooperation becomes universal habit, enabling true human freedom.

targetText: “bourgeois law” is not abolished in its entirety, but only in part, only in proportion to the economic revolution so far attained, i.e., only in respect of the means of production.
summary: Lenin elucidates that while socialism socializes the means of production, it must still distribute consumer goods according to labor performed, meaning an element of bourgeois law and inequality persists until higher communism.

targetText: under communism there remains for a time not only bourgeois law, but even the bourgeois state, without the bourgeoisie!
summary: Lenin highlights the dialectical paradox of the lower phase of communism: the state remains necessary to safeguard common property and equal distribution of labor, even after the capitalist class has been expropriated.

targetText: From each according to his ability, to each according to his needs!
summary: Lenin invokes Marx's famous principle of higher communism, explaining that it becomes achievable only when labor is no longer a mere means of life but life's prime want, and the productive forces have expanded to ensure abundance.
